issue: The in-plot annotation 'causal-triangle quad term overtakes linear ~106.8K' carries an arrow that points to a location INSIDE the plotted area, but the left-panel x-axis only runs to 1e2 = 100K. The true causal crossover (106.8K) is off-scale, so at the right edge the blue dash-dot causal-quadratic line is still BELOW the red linear line and no crossing is actually drawn. The arrow therefore implies a visible overtaking that the plot does not show, inviting a reader to infer the blue line crosses the red line within the plotted range (~100K).
evidence: Note 22.1-1 (printed 382) derives causal L* = N/(n_layers·d) = 70e9/(80·8192) ≈ 106.8K. Recompute at the axis limit x=100K: linear 2·N·L = 2·70e9·1e5 = 1.4e16 = 14.0 PFLOP; causal quad 2·n_layers·L²·d = 2·80·(1e5)²·8192 = 1.31e16 = 13.1 PFLOP. Linear > causal-quad at 100K, so the crossover (106.8K) lies beyond the 1e2 axis tick. The drawn blue line is below the red line at the right edge; the annotation arrow nonetheless lands on in-plot coordinates.
acceptance_test: Either (a) extend the left-panel x-axis to ≥1.2e2 so the 106.8K crossing is rendered and the arrow points at the actual intersection, or (b) reword the annotation to 'would overtake at ~106.8K (off-scale)' and aim the arrow at the right edge / outside the axes. Verify in the rendered panel that at x=1e2 the blue causal line is below the red linear line and that no in-plot crossing is suggested.

issue: Grayscale distinguishability: the two SOLID curves — 'linear 2·N·L' (red) and 'quadratic 4·n_layers·L²·d' (purple) — share the same line style and have close grayscale luminance. Because they cross at ~53.4K, a B&W reader can lose track of which solid line is which across the crossover without repeatedly consulting the legend, weakening the figure's core message (quadratic overtaking linear).
evidence: Legend lists both as solid; at x=1K linear (0.14 PFLOP) > quad (0.026 PFLOP), at x=100K linear (14) < quad-full (26.2), so the two solid lines intersect near 53.4K. In a grayscale render red→dark-mid gray and purple→mid gray, with identical dash pattern.
acceptance_test: In a grayscale render, a reader can follow the linear and the full-square quadratic curves across the entire x-range (including through the ~53.4K crossover) without the legend — e.g., by giving one of the two solid lines a distinct dash pattern or by adding short on-curve labels at the low-x and high-x ends.

issue: Visual-semantics / legend conflict: the horizontal reference line 'canonical peak = 40 rps' is drawn in the SAME blue dashed style that the legend assigns to the efficiency-adjusted capacity C_eff. A reader who consults the legend and sees a dashed-blue line flat at y=40 across the whole width can misread it as 'C_eff = 40 everywhere', even though C_eff is the rising dashed curve (e.g., ≈59 at N=30).
evidence: Legend: 'efficiency-adjusted capacity C_eff = 0.95 × C_analytic' = blue dashed. The flat 40 rps guide line is also blue dashed. C_eff(30) = 0.95·30·(17/8.6) ≈ 59.3, not 40, so the flat dashed line is not C_eff.
acceptance_test: The flat 40 rps reference line uses a style that does NOT appear in the legend (e.g., a thin solid gray line), so the legend's dashed-blue maps unambiguously to C_eff only; the 'canonical peak = 40 rps' label remains attached to the reference line.

issue: Figure/caption mismatch on gate placement: the caption states the six gates 'align with the transition seams', but the figure draws each gate box centered UNDER its stage (linked by a vertical dotted line), with the PASS/FAIL logic hanging below the stage rather than on the inter-stage seam arrows. A reader looking for gates on the transitions (the green arrows between boxes) finds none there.
evidence: Caption: 'Six gates align with the transition seams: PASS permits the next stage...'. Rendered figure: gate boxes (Data src valid, Train cost ok, ...) sit in a row beneath the stage row, each vertically aligned under one stage and connected by a dotted line; the forward seam arrows between stage boxes carry no gate.
acceptance_test: Either reword the caption to 'one gate per stage, gating the transition out of that stage' (matching the under-stage layout), or reposition the six gate boxes onto the inter-stage arrows so the drawn layout literally matches 'transition seams'.
